root_cause.text: Missing synchronization between the device removal path and the asynchronous dump_work workqueue, allowing mt7996_mac_dump_work() to dereference crash_data after it has been freed by mt7996_coredump_unregister().
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `cancel_work_sync(&dev->dump_work)` at the beginning of `mt7996_unregister_device()`, before `mt7996_coredump_unregister()` is called. This ensures the dump_work workqueue is fully canceled and synchronized before the crash_data structure is deallocated. The race condition diagram in the CVE description shows that without this synchronization, CPU 1 executing mt7996_mac_dump_work() can access the freed crash_data after CPU 0 has already called vfree() on it in mt7996_coredump_unregister().

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel pending dump_work during device unregistration to prevent use-after-free errors.
intent_record.what: Added a single line `cancel_work_sync(&dev->dump_work);` at the beginning of the mt7996_unregister_device() function, before the existing cancel_work_sync() call for wed_rro.work.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that any pending dump_work queued work is cancelled and waited for completion before the device unregistration proceeds. Without this, the dump_work could potentially execute after device resources are freed, causing use-after-free or null pointer dereference issues during device cleanup.
